newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Singapore leader Lee under fire from Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Singapore leader Lee under fire from Malaysia.

text.p: Staging a rare protest against a neighbour, Malaysian youths on Thursday waved placards insulting Singapore elder statesman Lee Kuan Yew and demanded he apologise for calling a Malaysian state "notorious".

Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad smiled as he shook hands with youths carrying placards that attacked Lee for saying in a Singapore court deposition on January 27 that Johor state was "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".
More than 100 members of the youth wing of Mahathir's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) hurled insults at Lee in a demonstration in Johor Baru.

They carried placards reading in English: "Kuan Yew stupid", "Mr. Lee you are senile", "Kuan Yew bloody idiot" "Kuan Yew must apologise". One placard in Malay read: "Kuan Yew is cursed. You are a pig. You've lost your mind".
The language was extraordinary in the usually circumspect ties among Southeast Asian neighbours.
Mahathir said Lee, the 73-year-old former Singapore Prime Minister who now serves as Senior Minister, should make amends for his remarks about Johor state.
"The feeling among a lot of people in Malaysia is that some way or another he should make amends," Mahathir told reporters in Johor Baru, which lies just across a causway from Singapore.

Lee's affidavit was filed in one of 13 libel lawsuits brought against Singapore opposition politician Tang Liang Hong after elections in January. Tang had fled to Johor, saying he had received death threats in Singapre.
Lee questioned whether Tang would be safer in Johor.
The Malaysian foreign ministry on Wednesday demanded an apology and a retraction of Lee's remarks.
In Kuala Lumpur, Human Resources Minister Lim Ah Lek urged Malaysian workers in Singapore to return home, the national Bernama news agency reported.

"Malaysia would like them to work here rather than elsewhere because we are having (labour-short) problems, especially now when the Singapore government does not seem to value our good relationship," he said.
The opposition Democratic Action Party said it would move a parliamentary motion condemning Singapore if there was no public apology and withdrawal of the remarks.
Singapore had no immediate comment, and no official in Lee's office was available to talk about the uproar.
Singapore shares were depressed on Thursday by the row with Malaysia and worse-than-expected economic numbers, dealers said.

"The row is the news of the day. It's kept people out of the market and given them an excuse to sell," said a local dealer as the benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended down 23.06 at 2,154.33, off 1.06 percent on the day.
Mahathir said the incident unmasked difficulties in ties between the two countries, which have had a simmering rivalry since Singapore left the Malaysian Federation in 1965.
"We have always had this problem," he said in reply to a question. "Although the public doesn't know very much, we've always had problems.
"We want to have friendly relations with Singapore. But to have friendly relations with Singapore requires considerable effort sometimes," he said.

Both Singapore and Malaysia are members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), which has practically made it a creed to avoid criticising its neighbours. ASEAN also includes Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam and Brunei.
Mistrust between Malaysia and Singapore is firmly rooted in history and culture, including the ethnic differences between largely Chinese Singapore and Malay-dominated Malaysia.

Last year the two countries had acrimonious exchanges when Lee raised the possibility of eventual reunification with Malaysia. Mahathir said then Singapore was using his country as a "bogeyman" to scare voters ahead of Singapore's January poll.
